business: ExceptionOS v0: production-impact intelligence for supplier delivery changes in Epicor manufacturers
by_segment: Purchasing or materials manager (owns the team and the shortage meeting)
COO, GM or owner of a 100-500 person manufacturer
Supply chain director or VP (owns OTIF, expedite cost, budget)
why_not: A free audit that wants our open POs, jobs and inventory sent to a startup I've never heard of is the first thing I'd question. Sending that data out needs IT and security sign-off, and I'd check with our Epicor partner before anything leaves the building, which won't happen within 30 days.

The audit is free, but it still means pulling PO, job and inventory data out of Epicor and handing it to an early-stage company I have never worked with. My IT and legal people would need to sign off on that, and my planners are already stretched, so I don't see this getting done inside 30 days.

Pulling clean Epicor exports is half a day of work I don't have, and sending PO and job data to an outside startup needs IT and my boss to sign off, which won't happen inside 30 days. I'd take a look if someone else did the export for me.
flip: Our Epicor partner vouches for them and IT approves the data handling in writing, plus a reference from a similar plant that caught a real supplier miss we had not already seen.
A written data-handling and deletion commitment that my IT team accepts, plus an export template my planner can run in under an hour.
A reference from another Epicor Kinetic shop of my size that I can call, plus a sample report run on dummy or last year's data so I can see the output before exposing live jobs.
A written security and data-handling one-pager, a commitment to delete the exports after the audit, and a reference from a plant that already ran the audit.
